markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of the student's own logged readings for one specimen (e.g. 'Specimen D: has a nucleus Yes; has chloroplasts Yes; classified Plantae').
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine readings consistent with the student's own Investigation Record rows; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('it is a plant') with no logged readings quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Links the specific evidence to the kingdom using the classification key: e.g. no nucleus means bacteria; nucleus plus cell wall plus chloroplasts means plant; nucleus plus cell wall but no chloroplasts means fungus; nucleus, no wall, single cell means protoctist; nucleus, no wall, many cells means animal.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct link from at least two pieces of evidence to the correct kingdom.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming the kingdom with no evidence, or using only appearance.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why another plausible kingdom is wrong using evidence (e.g. not a plant because it has no chloroplasts; not an animal because it has a cell wall; not bacteria because it has a nucleus).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct reason that excludes one other kingdom using a cell feature or how it gets food.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'it looks different' or 'it is not that one'.

markingScheme.criterion: States Kingdom Plantae and gives evidence from its cells: cell walls and chloroplasts (it makes its own food, an autotroph).
markingScheme.accept: Plantae with at least one correct piece of evidence (cell walls, chloroplasts, makes its own food).
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming a different kingdom, or Plantae with no evidence.

markingScheme.criterion: Identifies it as a seedless plant (like a moss or fern) because it reproduces with spores rather than seeds.
markingScheme.accept: Seedless plant (or moss/fern-type) with reference to spores or no seeds.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming gymnosperm or angiosperm, or 'a plant' with no type.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that a scientific name (genus and species) is universal: the same in every language, so scientists anywhere know exactly which organism is meant and can share information.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct reference to a universal or worldwide naming system avoiding confusion between languages or common names.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'it is a nice name' or 'so it has a name'.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's marking_scheme in marking_context: each point is worth the marks stated and is independent unless it names a dependsOn point; each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you exactly what does and doesn't count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points - the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity and vocabulary, never overlapping with the content marks. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy (5 marks = full; the Knowledge Check is adaptive, so the student answered one question per topic at their own level and each correct answer is 1 mark). Use the student's own logged Investigation Record (station/setting/reading/outcome columns in simulation_results.trials, especially the Mystery Cell Key and Kingdom Sorter rows) to check that any claim about their own readings is consistent with what they actually did. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording and do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 13 (5 auto + 3 + 3 + 2); report the percentage, one strength, one correction, and one next step, in under 80 words.
